answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable stake: every agent must lock a refundable deposit that only unlocks after a long history of useful work, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes as expensive as crossing a canyon on foot. Reputation then grows like a crystal, slowly, layer by layer, from attested contributions, and a newcomer with no history cannot borrow trust. Cheap identities stay worthless; only proven, staked agents earn the right to transact at scale.
